competition-enforcement.mechanism: Under EU rules a dominant position is not illegal; abusing it is, for example by requiring customers to buy all or most of what they need from the dominant supplier. An investigation gathers evidence and may end in a decision ordering the conduct to stop, with remedies or fines, or in binding commitments without a finding of infringement, and decisions can be appealed. Until then, effects on rivals' access to customers and on customers' prices or choice are possibilities, not outcomes.

facts.text: The Commission opened a formal antitrust investigation, case AT.40893, into whether Omya abused a dominant position in the supply of calcium carbonates.
Omya, headquartered in Switzerland, is the largest supplier of calcium carbonates in the EEA and may hold a dominant position, the Commission says.
The practices investigated are exclusive purchasing obligations and exclusivity rebates, which give customers financial incentives to source all or most of their calcium carbonates from Omya.
Calcium carbonates are used as fillers and coating pigments in paper production, where they can reduce production costs and improve brightness, opacity, smoothness and printability.
The Commission says competitive supplies can lower input costs for paper mills and benefit buyers of paper and cardboard, including packaging used instead of single-use plastic.
There is no legal deadline for an antitrust investigation; opening one relieves national competition authorities of their competence over the practices.

content.headline: Commission investigates Omya's exclusive purchasing obligations and rebates in calcium carbonate supply to paper makers

implications.text: If the practices were found abusive and ended, rival suppliers could compete for paper mills' purchases, which may lower calcium carbonate costs for some mills.
Omya could face a decision ordering the practices to end, or could offer commitments, if the Commission's concerns are confirmed.

content.summary: The European Commission has opened a formal antitrust investigation into whether Omya, the largest supplier of calcium carbonates in the European Economic Area, abused a possible dominant position by requiring paper-industry customers to buy all or most of their calcium carbonates from it and by offering exclusivity rebates. Calcium carbonates are fillers and coating pigments in paper and cardboard. The Commission says the practices may have limited rivals' ability to compete; opening an investigation does not prejudge its outcome, and there is no legal deadline.
uncertainties: How long the investigation will take; there is no legal deadline.
The release gives no market shares, prices or volumes.

facts.text: Marrowby said the autumn of 2026 saw the longest vessel queue in the harbour's records; the speech cites a median wait of eleven days and 140 sailings cancelled between September and mid-October.
She cited Reserve Bank research that a prolonged berth shortage could leave up to 24% of container volume waiting offshore, and said two in five exporters rely on a single terminal.
The speech reports freight charges up 8.4% in September, after 5.9% in August, and says queues this autumn delayed deliveries to Northmere shops and factories.
Rail carries around one fifth of containers leaving the harbour, and trucks most of the rest, according to figures cited in the speech.
The speech cites a regional plan for about 6 billion marks of berth and rail investment through 2030, and a Reserve Bank estimate that terminal upgrades could lift port capacity by a fifth.
According to the 2026 shippers' survey cited by Marrowby, carriers gave priority to long-contract customers and reduced space for spot bookings.

credit-conditions.mechanism: The cost and availability of external finance, such as bank loans and credit lines, matter for firms' ability to invest, hold inventories and hire. Surveys of firms, such as the ECB's survey on the access to finance of enterprises, ask firms about their need for external financing, its availability and its terms, by firm size, sector and country. Tighter reported conditions may mean that some firms postpone spending, especially those that rely on bank credit.

economics.main_uncertainty: Whether the tightening persists: the survey's sample changed substantially this round, and its balances are firms' reports, not measured lending rates or volumes.

significance.text: The survey reports a larger balance of firms reporting higher loan rates and a negative balance for loan availability. These are net percentages of respondents, not changes in measured interest rates or loan volumes. The ECB reports a positive bank-loan financing gap, which may matter for firms relying on bank finance if tighter reported conditions persist.

facts.text: A net 46% of firms reported higher interest rates on bank loans in the third quarter of 2026, against 42% in the previous quarter; large firms reported increases more often (net 55%) than SMEs (net 38%).
Firms reported lower availability of bank loans (net -5%, against -1%), while a net 2% reported lower bank loan needs; the ECB's financing gap indicator was positive, at net 2%.
Firms continued to see the general economic outlook as the main factor constraining the availability of external financing (net 31%, against 29%).
More firms expect the availability of external financing to decrease over the next three months.
First-time respondents were the majority of this round's 12,822 enterprises, which the ECB says makes the numerical questions challenging to interpret at this stage.

content.headline: Euro area firms report costlier bank loans and lower loan availability in the third quarter, ECB survey shows

implications.text: Firms that rely on bank loans could face higher borrowing costs and less credit, which may weigh on their investment or inventory plans if the tightening persists.
Large firms reporting rate increases more often than SMEs might mean the tightening is not confined to smaller borrowers.

missing: Country-level results, on the ECB Data Portal, were not retrieved.
Measured bank lending rates and volumes for the same quarter.
content.summary: In the ECB's Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises for the third quarter of 2026, a net 46% of euro area firms reported higher interest rates on bank loans, against 42% in the previous quarter, and firms reported that the availability of bank loans fell by more than their needs, widening the financing gap. The ECB says that, with first-time respondents the majority of this round's sample, the answers to numerical questions such as price and inflation expectations are hard to interpret for now.
uncertainties: The release does not say whether the change in the sample also affects the balances on loan conditions.
Net percentages are survey balances, not measured lending rates or volumes.
